bonus_mechanics: Federal bonus flows through federal AGI (100% for property acquired after 19 Jan 2025; 40% earlier). Act 11 (R.S. 47:297.25) adds an elective state deduction for 100% of the cost of qualified property and qualified improvement property (168(k) and 168(e)(6) as in effect 1 Jan 2024) in the year placed in service; Schedule E code 32E deducts the amount exceeding federal depreciation, and Line 2E adds back federal depreciation on that property in later years. Cannot duplicate federal depreciation. Form R-90158 attached.
change_note: Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session: new elective Louisiana full expensing for tax periods beginning on or after 1 Jan 2025 (RIB 25-012; 2025 IT-540 instructions). It predates OBBBA and is not a response to Pub. L. 119-21.
special_rules: The state election defines qualified property by 168(k) as of 1 Jan 2024, so 168(n) property is not within the state election's definition, but no add-back of the federal 168(n) deduction appears on the 2025 Schedule E. Pass-through-entity-tax election (R.S. 47:287.732.2) shifts income to entity level.

bonus_mechanics: Decoupled. Addition (36 MRSA 5122(1)(KK)): net increase in depreciation attributable to the 168(k) deduction, i.e. federal depreciation minus the depreciation that would have been allowed without bonus, in the year placed in service. Subtraction (5122(2)(RR)) in later years: depreciation allowable without bonus minus federal depreciation each year; total subtraction cannot exceed the addition; any remaining recapture is allowed on disposition.
special_rules: Recapture follows the asset's normal MACRS schedule, so a no-bonus depreciation schedule must be kept per asset. Pass-through owners limit the addition and later subtraction by the federal passive-loss or at-risk limitation percentage. Maine Capital Investment Credit of 1.2% of the addition for property placed in service in tax years beginning 2020 and later (per the May 2022 guidance). Fiscal-year filers use the year the fiscal year begins.
source_citation: MRS Guidance Document, Modifications Related to Bonus Depreciation & Section 179 Expensing (rev. May 2022), Part 1; 36 MRSA 5122(1)(KK), (2)(RR)

bonus_mechanics: Permanent decoupling for a taxpayer that is not a manufacturing entity (TG 10-210.1): compute 167(a) depreciation without the 168(k) allowance. Add the 168(k) allowance back to federal AGI in the year claimed, then subtract it ratably in later years per the property's depreciation method over the recovery period. Requires pro forma federal returns without the allowance; reported on Form 500DM.
special_rules: A manufacturing entity (defined in TG 10-210.1 under the 2017 More Jobs for Marylanders Act; definition not read) takes federal 167(a), 168(k) and 179 unmodified for property placed in service on or after 1 Jan 2019, and files no 500DM for that. All taxpayers must apply the 280F limits to heavy-duty SUVs as if rated 6,000 lb GVWR or less (TG 10-210.1(5)). Section 179 under state law ignores any change to 179 made after 31 Dec 2002: 25,000 reduced dollar for dollar above 200,000. Automatic temporary decoupling (TG 10-108) from federal changes costing 5,000,000 or more, for tax years beginning in the year of enactment.
